Phainon hummed like he saw right through him, trailing lazy kisses along his neck before pulling back. “Stay in bed today,” he said simply, almost like an order.

Mydei arched a brow, glancing over at him with a faint smirk. “Why?”

“So I can make breakfast,” Phainon replied, surprisingly straightforward. He brushed a strand of hair from Mydei’s face, blue eyes dim in the soft morning light. “You don’t move until you’ve rested. I’ll take care of you.”

“Sunshine, I have a ‘no-Phainon-allowed’ sign on your kitchen door.”

“Why don’t you trust me in there?”

“You almost burnt it down last time.”

Phainon pouted and gave him puppy eyes, hoping it would help in changing his opinion. “Please?”

The honesty in his tone made Mydei’s chest tighten. He almost wanted to roll his eyes again, to tease him like always, but instead he let out a quiet breath and sank deeper into the sheets. “…Fine. But if you burn anything, I’m not eating it.”

“Yay!” Phainon beamed.

“Look at this grown ass man saying ‘yay!’ as if he didn’t rearrange my guts last night,” Mydei made fun of him, slapping a hand on his back. “Go. And brush your teeth too. Your morning breath stinks, don’t even think about kissing me.”

Phainon grinned in mischief, pressing a kiss to his lips before untangling himself from the bed. Mydei watched him move across the room, tugging on a loose shirt, and despite the soreness weighing down his body, a soft warmth curled in his chest.

“I said to brush your teeth before kissing me, Phainon!”
